hub.title: Tools
hub.lead: Read specifications, size transformers, prepare inquiries: RITZ tools take care of the routine work – and save the back-and-forth between engineering, purchasing and sales.
hub.privacy: All tools run in your browser. Texts, files and results only leave your device when you send an inquiry.

assistant.text: Paste a tender, an email or an Excel list: the check reads items, quantities and technical data, finds matching RITZ types and pre-configures them.
assistant.saves: Instead of comparing datasheets item by item: results in seconds.

calculators.text: Lead burden, effective security and accuracy limit factor, short-circuit rating, primary current and voltage transformers – with a traceable calculation and standard references.

assist.title: Specification check
assist.lead: Paste tender text, an email, rating plate data or an Excel list. The check recognises items and technical data, suggests matching RITZ transformers and fills in the configurator.
assist.inputLabel: Text of the inquiry, tender or list
assist.placeholder: e.g. Item 1: 3 pcs current transformer, indoor, Um 24 kV, 400/5/5 A, 0.5 FS5 15 VA, 5P20 10 VA, Ith 25 kA 1 s, 50 Hz
assist.fileHint: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, GAEB or text – drag and drop works too

calc.title: Transformer calculators
calc.lead: Five calculators for everyday sizing of current and voltage transformers – with the calculation path, standard references and a direct route to the matching product.

tabText.burden: Burden of leads and devices, suitable rated output
tabText.factor: Effective FS or ALF at the actual burden
tabText.short: Ith and Idyn from the short-circuit current
tabText.primary: Rated primary current from load and margin
tabText.vt: Ratio, voltage factor and voltage drop

calc.useBurden: Use in the security factor calculator

burden.k2: Go and return conductor (single-phase, earth fault)
burden.devHint: Sum of meter, transducer and relay
burden.low25: The operating burden is below 25 % of the rated output. The error limits of the metering classes apply between 25 % and 100 % of the rated burden (IEC 61869-2) – choose a lower rated output or add an additional burden.
burden.alt1A: With a 1 A secondary current, the same lead would only cause {v} – on long leads, 1 A pays off.
burden.over: The burden exceeds common rated outputs. Consider a larger cross-section, a shorter lead or a 1 A secondary current.
burden.basis: R = k · ρ · l / A with ρ(Cu, 20 °C) = 0.0175 Ω·mm²/m, ρ(Al) = 0.0286 Ω·mm²/m and temperature coefficient; S = I² · R. Error limits to IEC 61869-2.

factor.sbHint: e.g. from the lead burden calculator
factor.rctHint: From the test report; typically 0.1–0.4 Ω at 5 A, 2–10 Ω at 1 A
factor.fsHigh: At the actual burden the instrument security factor rises to {v}: connected meters are exposed to correspondingly higher currents during a short circuit. Choose a rated output close to the operating burden or add an additional burden of {add}.
factor.fsOk: The effective instrument security factor stays within the rating.
factor.alfOk: The effective accuracy limit factor covers the maximum short-circuit current.
factor.alfLow: The effective accuracy limit factor is not sufficient for the maximum short-circuit current: choose a higher ALF, a higher rated output or a lower burden.
factor.alfInfo: Enter the maximum short-circuit current and the primary current to check the protection core.
factor.basis: n' = n · (Si + Sr) / (Si + Sb) with Si = Isr² · Rct (IEC 61869-2).

short.mult: Ith as a multiple of Ipr
short.multHigh: Above 100 × Ipr, the thermal short-time current becomes demanding for transformers with a wound primary – consider a higher primary current, a bar primary or contact our sales team.
short.idynOk: The standard value Idyn = {f} × Ith covers the peak short-circuit current.
short.idynLow: The peak short-circuit current ({ip}) exceeds {f} × Ith – state Idyn ≥ {ip} in the inquiry.
short.trafoNote: Simplified calculation without network impedance (infinite bus) – on the safe side.
short.basis: Ith(1 s) = Ik″ · √tk; ip = κ · √2 · Ik″ (IEC 60909); Idyn = 2.5 · Ith at 50 Hz or 2.6 · Ith at 60 Hz (IEC 61869-1).

primary.series: next value of the standard series ≥ Imin
primary.sClass: The operating current is below 20 % of the primary current. For accurate metering at partial load, choose S classes (0.2S, 0.5S) – they are specified from 1 % of the rated current.
primary.over: The operating current exceeds the rated current including the extension.
primary.ok: The operating current is within the range of highest accuracy (20–120 % of the rated current).
primary.extNote: With an extended rated current of {e}, the transformer may be operated continuously at up to {i}.
primary.basis: Ib = S / (√3 · U) or S / U; standard series of rated primary currents 10–12.5–15–20–25–30–40–50–60–75 A and their decimal multiples (IEC 61869-2).

vt.isolated: Isolated or resonant earthed, without tripping
vt.shareNote: The voltage drop of the lead adds to the ratio error of the transformer: it uses {v} of the error limit of class {c}.
vt.shareHigh: More than a quarter of the error limit is lost in the lead – provide a larger cross-section or a shorter lead.
vt.vfNote: Voltage factor to IEC 61869-3 for the selected neutral earthing.
vt.enNote: In open-delta connection, the residual winding provides the displacement voltage for earth-fault detection.
vt.basis: Upr = Un/√3 (single-pole); voltage factors and secondary voltages to IEC 61869-3; ΔU = I · 2 · ρ · l / A.
